kyoto_minatoya_kosodate_ame.gf_detail: Ask. One hard candy made from malt syrup and sugar; one reviewer read the label as malt sugar from sweet potato and corn, but no gluten information is published (official site; reviews).
kyoto_minatoya_kosodate_ame.vegan_detail: Ask. A candy of malt syrup and granulated sugar, and loose Uji tea; ingredients beyond that are not published (reviews; official site).
kyoto_minatoya_kosodate_ame.hours_raw: 10:00–16:00, every day of the year; open later during Rokudo Mairi (Tabelog); may close for sudden events (official site, January 2026). Takeaway only — a small counter shop with no seating. Cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). The small 75 g bag often sells out early; ask the shop to hold one (official site). On Matsubara-dori east of Yamato-oji, at Rokudo no Tsuji, 2 min walk from Rokuharamitsu-ji, 10 min from Keihan Kiyomizu-Gojo Stn (official site).
kyoto_minatoya_kosodate_ame.notes: [Candy shop · Rokuhara, by Rokuharamitsu-ji] A tiny shop that sells one thing: amber malt-syrup candy, broken by hand, tied to a 1599 legend of a dead mother whose ghost came nightly to buy candy for the baby born in the grave. The shop calls itself Japan's oldest candy maker, over 450 years old. A bag is ¥700 (¥400 small), with Uji teas beside it — a gentle sweetness and a story to take home. Open daily 10:00–16:00; cash only.

roles: Family shop, people not named (official site signs as みなとや一同)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: Japan’s longest-established candy shop, over 450 years old; the legend: in Keicho 4 (1599) a wife of the 江村 family was buried, and days later a baby’s cry was heard from the grave — the child of the dead wife; a woman had come every night to buy candy and stopped once the child was dug out; the child became a monk at eight and a renowned priest, dying at 68 in 1666; the candy came to be called the ghost’s child-rearing candy. The shop has supplied its candy to はぐくみハッピーギフト, a Higashiyama ward gift for new parents, and received a letter of thanks (official site, March 2021). Candy and tea are made by hand (official site, September 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: to keep passing on the story of “the candy that carried a life”.

anecdotes.text: An August 2025 first-timer was told by the staff that the ghost first came 426 years ago.
A December 2025 regular notes the legend is said to have inspired GeGeGe no Kitaro.
A September 2025 visitor bought a bag as a gift for a couple expecting a baby.

cultural_comfort.note: Takeaway counter; cash only.

kyoto_shinshindo_kyodai_kitamonmae.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a bakery café — rolls, sandwiches, toast, cream puffs and curry (2025–26 reviews).

kyoto_shinshindo_kyodai_kitamonmae.hours_raw: Mon and Wed–Sun 10:00–18:00 (last order 17:30); closed Tuesday (Tabelog). rurubu also lists 10:00–18:00, closed Tuesday. Order at the counter, then sit (May 2026 review). No bookings; cash only — no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). No photos inside: signs on the door and in the room (Tabelog; November 2025–August 2026 reviews). 100 seats at long wooden tables, with tables kept for students and a student discount on coffee with a university ID (November 2025 and February 2026 reviews; a May 2026 diner was told the discount needs the whole party to be university students). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Facing Kyoto University's north gate; 10 min from Demachiyanagi Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_shinshindo_kyodai_kitamonmae.notes: [1930 student café · Kyoto University north gate] Kyoto's "second university library": a Paris-inspired café opened in 1930, with massive wooden tables by the craftsman Kuroda Tatsuaki, a courtyard, and students reading over a single blend coffee, curry or a sandwich. About ¥1,000. Cash only; no photos inside; closed Tuesday.

chef_bio.background: Opened in 1930 as a French-style café by the bakery 進々堂, which began in 1913 and was the first in Kyoto to sell French bread; the founder, 続木斉, had studied bread-making in Paris and modelled the café on those in the Latin Quarter, hoping Japanese students would also learn Western esprit (serai.jp). The long one-piece tables and benches were commissioned from the woodworker 黒田辰秋 so many students could sit at once (serai.jp; rurubu; November 2025 review). The fourth-generation proprietor 川口聡 says the café's atmosphere stays the same because of the founding ideals (serai.jp, undated). Operator: rurubu says the café is now a separate corporation from the 進々堂 bakery, and the bakery's own shop list does not include it; 2026 reviewers still call it a branch of the Kyoto bakery chain (May and September 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: "The air of the shop stays the same even as the times and the town change, because of the founding ideals" (川口聡, serai.jp).
chef_bio.specialty: Blend coffee; curry rice set; sandwiches.

anecdotes.text: In October 2025 a visitor returned after about 50 years, reading a maths and physics book bought at a nearby bookshop over black coffee.
A November 2025 visitor on the way to Ginkaku-ji found the sandwiches sold out, took the roll-bread brunch set, and found the staff's indifference very Kyoto.
A November 2025 visitor was told that lingering was not allowed before noon, and felt the many notices spoiled the calm.

kyoto_hatoya_shokudo.notes: [Diner · Higashioji Marutamachi, home cooking from 6 am] A long-running diner facing Kumano Shrine, open from dawn: order a pork miso soup, sake-lees soup or udon, then pick a couple of home-style sides — grilled mackerel, chilled tofu, rolled egg — from the trays, for under ¥1,000. Cash only; no children; closed Saturday.

roles: Owner (unnamed), who serves from the side-dish trays (February 2026)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a cafeteria-style diner at the Higashioji Marutamachi crossing. A December 2025 reviewer read online that it has been in business for over 70 years.
chef_bio.specialty: Pork miso soup set; pick-your-own sides.

anecdotes.text: An April 2026 morning jogger stopped for a kitsune udon set with simmered mackerel, ¥900 in all.
A November 2025 visitor hunting for an early-opening breakfast found it and parked behind Kumano Shrine.
An October 2026 visitor noted how hard it is to find ordinary home cooking out, and why regulars might come daily.

The kawadoko (river terrace) moves indoors if rain is likely, and wet terrace or kotatsu-terrace seats move indoors (Tabelog); terrace seating ran to the end of October in 2026 (October 2026). Service charge 10% (Tabelog, Japanese text: 「サービス料10％」). Cards incl. UnionPay; QR incl. Alipay and WeChat Pay; no e-money (Tabelog). 60 seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). The eighth house on the east side of Pontocho north of Shijo; 2 min from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn (Tabelog). No children’s menu (September 2026).
kyoto_nagamegawa_pontocho.notes: [Kyoto cuisine · Pontocho, kaiseki on the river terrace] A Pontocho house with a kawadoko over the Kamo River that stays open to the end of October: a ¥4,840 mini kaiseki with Omi beef sukiyaki at lunch, summer kaiseki (¥6,600) with yuba, hamo and yudofu, or indoor seats with a river view. 10% service. Preschool children only in private rooms; no kids menu.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a Japanese, tofu and sukiyaki restaurant on Pontocho with river-terrace and kotatsu-terrace seating.

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 diner was glad the terrace was still open at month’s end, when neighbours had closed theirs by mid-October.
An October 2026 overseas visitor was glad a first taste of Kyoto cuisine came here, and the friends all loved it.
A September 2026 parent noted there is no children’s menu, calling the terrace kaiseki a place for adults.

kyoto_tairiki_tei_nanzenji.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: homemade wheat udon and tempura (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_tairiki_tei_nanzenji.vegan_detail: Not vegan: udon in dashi with chicken and burdock tempura (2026 reviews).
kyoto_tairiki_tei_nanzenji.hours_raw: 11:30–20:00, open all year (Tabelog). Dinner reservations are for courses only (official site); at lunch, expect a queue from before opening with numbered tickets (October–November 2026). Cancellation on the day costs 100%, and switching from a course to à la carte after arriving is charged at the course price (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). 47 seats: counters facing the garden, tables, private room (Tabelog; October 2026). Non-smoking; smoking area outside (Tabelog). 1 min from the main gate of Nanzen-ji; 9 min from Keage Stn (Tabelog). First anniversary celebrated in January 2025 (official site).
kyoto_tairiki_tei_nanzenji.notes: [Udon and café · Nanzen-ji, a garden view with lunch] A restaurant a minute from Nanzen-ji’s gate whose counters look out on a Japanese garden: homemade udon with Awa-chicken or burdock tempura (¥1,600–1,700), dango you toast yourself and matcha latte. Very popular — a numbered queue forms before 11:30. Dinner is courses only, by reservation. Open daily.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: a restaurant with a seasonal Japanese garden view and homemade udon, which marked its first anniversary in January 2025 with maiko dances; dinner reservations are for courses only. An October 2026 reviewer says the garden was designed by an 11th-generation gardener of the Ogawa line.

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 visitor arrived at 11:00 and saw a queue form quickly; only courses could be booked.
A September 2026 café visitor enjoyed toasting dango at the table with a choice of toppings.
A November 2026 visitor arriving five minutes before opening was the 15th group in line.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: 四季折々の絶景の庭園、職人の自家製うどん、ディナーの予約はコースのみ、2025年1月に開店1周年の舞妓の舞。食べログ: うどん・ステーキ・カフェ、左京区南禅寺草川町81、南禅寺の正門から徒歩1分、蹴上駅から徒歩9分、11:30〜20:00、無休、予約可 (当日キャンセル100%、来店後のコースからの変更もコース料金)、カード・電子マネー・QR 可、47席、禁煙 (外に喫煙所)。口コミ (2026年9月〜11月、英語): Awa の鶏と舞茸の天ぷらうどん1,700円、大きなごぼう天うどん1,600円、自分で焼く団子、抹茶ラテ、庭に面したカウンター、開店前から整理券の行列。

cultural_comfort.note: Queue for a numbered ticket at lunch; dinner is courses by reservation. Many overseas visitors (November 2026). No English evidence found.

kyoto_takoyaki_kohaku_takano.gf_detail: Not GF: takoyaki in a batter of domestic wheat (2025 reviews).
kyoto_takoyaki_kohaku_takano.vegan_detail: Not vegan: octopus takoyaki in a dashi batter, topped with bonito flakes (2024–2025 reviews).
kyoto_takoyaki_kohaku_takano.hours_raw: Tuesday–Sunday 12:00–20:00; closed Monday (Tabelog). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, JCB), iD and QR incl. PayPay (Tabelog). 4 standing places at the counter; takeaway; non-smoking (Tabelog). Order inside, past a plastic curtain (November 2025). At the corner of Kitaoji and Higashioji by the Takano bus stop; about 6 min walk from Chayama Stn (Tabelog; November 2025). Sometimes runs a kitchen car at events (May 2025).
kyoto_takoyaki_kohaku_takano.notes: [Takoyaki · Takano, by Kitaoji-Higashioji] A stylish little stand making additive-free takoyaki with domestic wheat and a dashi-rich batter — fluffy and creamy, with big pieces of octopus — in flavours from classic sauce and Kyoto sesame to negi-dashi soy, salsa and pesto. Order as few as three. One August 2026 visitor found the balls seemingly pre-cooked, with a hard skin. Closed Monday.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a takoyaki shop at Takano with a website at takoyaki-kohaku.com; registered as an official listing by the shop. Reviewers describe an owner who chooses ingredients carefully, additive-free takoyaki of domestic wheat (2024–2025), and a kitchen car at an organic market event (May 2025).

anecdotes.text: In May 2025 the shop ran a kitchen car at an organic-store anniversary event, with about fifteen people queuing.
A July 2024 fan called it the best takoyaki ever and pleaded for a Tokyo branch.
An August 2026 visitor ordering salt and sesame oil found the balls seemingly pre-cooked, with a hard skin.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: たこ焼き、左京区高野東開町11-1、叡山電鉄茶山駅から徒歩約6分、市バス「高野」すぐ、火〜日 12:00〜20:00、月曜定休、予約可、カード (VISA・JCB)・iD・QR 可、立ち食い4名 (カウンター)、テイクアウト、禁煙。口コミ (2024年7月〜2026年8月、英語): 北大路と東大路の角、無添加、国産小麦、だしのきいた生地、ふわとろ、大きなたこ、6個700円、ソース、京風ごまだれ、ねぎだし醤油、塩とごま油、サルサ、ジェノベーゼ、3個から注文可、イベントのキッチンカー、作り置きで皮が硬かったとの声 (2026年8月)。

kyoto_kiraku_toei_uzumasa.gf_detail: Not GF: wheat ramen and tsukemen, curry ramen, fried chicken (2024–2025 reviews).
kyoto_kiraku_toei_uzumasa.vegan_detail: Not vegan: meat broths, chashu, shumai and meat-wrapped rice balls (2024–2025 reviews).
kyoto_kiraku_toei_uzumasa.hours_raw: Inside Toei Kyoto Studio Park (Toei Uzumasa Eigamura) — park admission is needed, and re-entry is not allowed (Tabelog; February 2025). 9:00–17:00 from 1 March to 30 November, 9:30–16:00 from 1 December to 28 February; closed 24–31 December; hours may change (Tabelog). Reservations for groups only (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). 52 seats; non-smoking; parking at the park (Tabelog). 5 min walk from Uzumasa-Koryuji Stn, 13 min from JR Uzumasa Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_kiraku_toei_uzumasa.notes: [Ramen · inside Toei Kyoto Studio Park, Uzumasa] A family-friendly ramen canteen inside the Edo-period film-set park — you need a park ticket to eat here, with no re-entry. Curry ramen, Mito Komon-themed ramen with garlic and ginger to stir in, cold tsukemen, kids sets and collaboration specials, at prices lower than the park's other restaurants. One guest found the miso broth watery. Daytime only.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a ramen and tsukemen restaurant inside Toei Uzumasa Eigamura, with seasonal hours. Reviewers describe one of several eateries in the park, cheaper than the rest, with collaboration menus tied to park events (2024–2025).

anecdotes.text: A February 2025 family, finding other park restaurants priced at ¥1,500–2,000 a set and unable to leave and re-enter, settled here for an ¥800 miso ramen.
A February 2024 Setsubun visitor with family found the curry ramen mild enough for children.
A February 2024 guest found the outside menu display did not match the sets offered inside.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: ラーメン・つけ麺、右京区太秦東蜂ヶ岡町10 東映太秦映画村内、JR太秦駅から徒歩13分、太秦広隆寺駅から徒歩5分、3月1日〜11月30日 9:00〜17:00、12月1日〜2月28日 9:30〜16:00、12月24日〜31日休み、団体のみ予約可、カード・電子マネー・QR 可、52席、禁煙、駐車場あり。口コミ (2024年2月〜2025年10月、英語): 映画村の中 (入村料が必要、再入場不可)、ほかの店より安い、太秦カレーラーメン900円、水戸藩ラーメン880円 (ねぎ、にら、らっきょう、にんにく、生姜)、味噌ラーメン800円、冷やしつけ麺、ラーメンとせいろのセット、唐揚げ定食、中華蒸し物の定食 (中華そば、焼売、ちまき)、お子様ラーメンセット800円、肉巻きおにぎり、エヴァンゲリオンや水戸黄門のコラボメニュー、味噌のスープが薄いとの声。

kyoto_m_and_maison_gojo.gf_detail: Ask. Japanese breakfast sets of grilled fish, small vegetable dishes, tamagoyaki, sesame tofu, miso soup and rice; side dishes are not explained in detail (2026 reviews).
kyoto_m_and_maison_gojo.vegan_detail: Not vegan: sets centre on grilled or raw fish, tamagoyaki and dashi-based miso soup (2026 reviews).
kyoto_m_and_maison_gojo.hours_raw: Monday–Friday 8:00–15:00; Saturday–Sunday 7:30–15:00; last order 14:30; irregular closing days (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, online; advised for holiday mornings (Tabelog; September 2026). English menu (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR (Tabelog). 22 seats: 6 at the counter and one table on the 1F, three tables on the 2F; non-smoking; coin parking next door (Tabelog). A tiled roof and a wooden sign with a fish mark on Rokujo-dori; 5 min walk from Gojo Stn, 10 from Kyoto Station (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_m_and_maison_gojo.notes: [Japanese breakfast · Rokujo by Gojo Stn] A tiled-roof restaurant near Kyoto Station serving a ryokan-style Japanese breakfast from 7:30 at weekends: grilled fish with miso soup and three or five seasonal small dishes, and a praised corn rice. A reviewer calls it the New York eatery OKONOMI brought back to Kyoto; English menu. Some find it a little pricey or average; one found the miso soup lukewarm. Book for holidays.

roles: Kitchen at the open counter and floor staff (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a breakfast set restaurant to experience the seasons of Kyoto; registered as an official listing by the operator. A November 2026 reviewer says it was born from bringing the New York Japanese eatery OKONOMI back to Kyoto; July 2026 reviewers note its popularity for breakfast.
chef_bio.philosophy: Experience the seasons of Kyoto at breakfast (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: A July 2026 guest wished the grilled corn rice were sold as onigiri, and likened the meal to a ryokan breakfast.
A September 2026 couple found the service attentive but the first miso soup lukewarm.
An October 2026 diner thought it aimed at inbound tourists, with no explanation of the side dishes and nothing especially Kyoto about it.

kyoto_sushitetsu_pontocho.gf_detail: Ask. À la carte nigiri with soy; small cooked dishes such as kinpira and ganmodoki as otoshi; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
kyoto_sushitetsu_pontocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a sushi bar; natto and egg are on the nigiri list, but most items are fish and shellfish (2026 reviews).
kyoto_sushitetsu_pontocho.hours_raw: Monday–Friday 17:00–24:00; Saturday, Sunday and holidays 12:00–24:00; last order 23:30; closed 31 December–1 January; hours can change with supply (Tabelog). Reservations only for tatami seating for 4 or more; otherwise write your name on the board and queue — a line of about 30 at 19:00 one September evening; a 60-minute last order (August 2026) or a 90-minute limit (October 2026). A seat fee of ¥324 (Tabelog original (御席料)324円); an appetizer (otoshi) is served (June and October 2026). Cards and QR; no e-money (Tabelog). 52 seats with counter, tables and tatami, some with a Kamo River view; non-smoking (Tabelog; September 2026). 1F of the Karafuneya Pontocho building, Pontocho south of Sanjo; 5 min walk from Sanjo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_sushitetsu_pontocho.notes: [Sushi · Pontocho on the Kamo River, queue and eat] A busy, cheerful sushi bar by the river where most nigiri — chutoro included — cost about ¥280 for two, plus wagyu sushi and fresh akagai; most reviewers spent ¥3,000–3,999. No bookings except tatami for four or more: write your name and wait, with time limits when busy. Table service can lag behind the counter. ¥324 seat fee. Open till midnight.

roles: Sushi chefs at the counter and floor staff (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a sushi bar in the Karafuneya Pontocho building, with hours that change with supply. Reviewers in 2026 describe long queues, a mix of Japanese and overseas guests, a pleasant chef, and prices only a little above conveyor-belt sushi.

anecdotes.text: A June 2026 diner noted that chutoro costs the same as natto and joked that this was unfair to the natto.
A September 2026 repeat visitor arrived 30 minutes before opening and was the seventh group in line.
At 19:00 in September 2026 there was a line of about thirty, half Japanese and half overseas visitors.

kyoto_minari_isetan.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: chijimi, cold noodles, japchae and gochujang- and soy-based sauces in the sets (2026 reviews).
kyoto_minari_isetan.vegan_detail: Ask: Tabelog lists vegetarian options and the menu is vegetable-led, but sets include meat soups, eggs and kimchi (2026 reviews).
kyoto_minari_isetan.hours_raw: Tabelog: daily 11:00–22:00 (last order 21:00); closed on JR Kyoto Isetan's closing days. Online booking only for up to 4, until the day before and for times up to 18:00; 5 or more by phone. Busy at weekend lunch — check the wait by QR code (May 2026). 45 seats (41 at tables, 4 on sofas), semi-private seating; non-smoking; wheelchair access; children welcome. Cards accepted; e-money only Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog).
kyoto_minari_isetan.notes: [Korean · Kyoto Station Isetan 11F, vegetable-heavy set meals] A calm Korean home-cooking room on JR Kyoto Isetan's restaurant floor: bibimbap, sundubu, samgyetang and bossam in sets of kimchi and little side dishes, mildly spiced and full of vegetables — easy off the train or with children. Diners found the set chijimi small or cold (June, September 2026) and the bossam pork tough (October 2026).

chef_bio.background: Reviewers in 2026 describe a spacious, semi-private room on the department store's restaurant floor, sweeter, mild seasoning that suited children, solo women and small groups, and fewer tourists than other Kyoto Station spots (June 2026). A 美菜莉 also runs on Ginza Mitsukoshi's 11th floor (LINE notice); an August 2026 diner mentions a popular Tokyo branch.

anecdotes.text: October 2026: "the pork was tougher than I expected, making it a bit difficult to chew… Also, the vegetables were unseasoned, so a little dipping sauce would have been appreciated."
June 2026: "I was surprised by the small size of the chijimi in the set."
June 2026: "overall, the flavors were on the sweeter side, which was comforting since we had elementary school kids with us."

kyoto_nijo_en.notes: [Tempura and oden · Nijo Station, a dashi-proud izakaya] A cosy two-floor izakaya by Nijo Station: a ten-kind tempura platter, oden in the house dashi, Kyoto vegetables with white miso, and a good list of less-common sake, with the owner chatting across the counter. Some found portions small and prices high (June, August 2026), and late in the evening much sells out. No service charge. Closed Thursday.

roles: Owner, not named in a source
chef_bio.background: Opened 9 April 2019 (Tabelog). Reviewers from 2023 to 2026 describe a cosy room where solo diners chat with the owner across the counter, staff who say "we pride ourselves on our dashi" (January 2024), attentive service, and an upstairs room used by families and groups.

anecdotes.text: January 2024: on the staff's recommendation — "We pride ourselves on our dashi" — the family chose oden.

kyoto_ching_ming_gion.vegan_detail: Not vegan: Cantonese-leaning meat and seafood dishes and set meals (2026 reviews).

Cards, transit IC and e-money, QR. 5th floor of the Yasaka Gion Building beside Yojiya; the entrance is behind a coffee shop (October 2026); window views over Hanamikoji.
kyoto_ching_ming_gion.notes: [Chinese · Gion, a 5th-floor view over Hanamikoji] The Kyoto branch of Osaka's 1967 Chinese house Ching-Ming, five floors above the Gion crossing with windows over Hanamikoji: a good-value ¥1,600 lunch gozen, eight-treasure yakisoba and shark-fin ramen at night. Regulars note shrinking portions (July–August 2026); some found the pre-made side dishes just okay (August 2026) and the room too cold. 10% service charge after 17:00.

roles: Not named in a source; branch of 青冥 (Ching-Ming)
chef_bio.background: 青冥 was founded in 1967 with its main shop in Dojima, Osaka (Ikyu listing); a 2026 recruiting page for 株式会社ミヨシコーポレーション lists 青冥 堂島本店, 祇園店, 阪急池田店 and 大丸梅田店. anecdotes.text: September 2026: "My late father often took me to the Chinmin in Umeda… He always ordered the Eight Treasure Yakisoba. This Kyoto branch was also incredibly delicious."

August 2026: "The freshly made sweet and sour pork was delicious, but the pre-made mapo tofu and stir-fried noodles with sauce were just okay."

kyoto_kroon_demachiyanagi.hours_raw: Tabelog lists no hours. Reviewers ate lunch sets (four choices) on weekdays and weekends at about 13:00, and dinner late in the evening (2024–2026). kyoto_kroon_demachiyanagi.notes: [Thai · Demachiyanagi, student-friendly lunch sets] A cosy 16-seat Thai restaurant on a lane by Demachiyanagi Station since 2008: pad Thai, green curry and kra pao rice lunch sets with fresh spring rolls, and spicy clams and shrimp skewers in the evening. One diner found the pad Thai too sweet and felt pushed to order drinks (January 2025). Cash only; smoking allowed per Tabelog.

chef_bio.background: Opened 28 June 2008 (Tabelog). Reviewers from 2024 to 2026 describe a counter and a few tables, a kitchen and a single front-of-house server, a warm welcome, and a spillover crowd from the omurice shop next door. Its former website address now opens the site of イーサン, a Thai restaurant at Imadegawa (fetched 6 November 2026).

anecdotes.text: January 2025: "The female staff member was energetic, but her demeanor felt a bit unfriendly, almost pressuring me to order drinks… the seasoning was on the sweeter side."
"Upon opening the door, I was transported to Thailand." — January 2025.

kyoto_lush_life_demachiyanagi.notes: [Jazz kissa · Demachiyanagi, coffee and records by the station] A nine-seat counter coffee-and-jazz shop under a striped awning at Demachiyanagi Station, lined with LPs: coffee, a firm old-fashioned pudding, curry and hayashi rice, and a drink on the terrace. anecdotes.text: February 2025: "Even though it's a jazz café, the atmosphere is relaxed enough for casual conversations… On the day I visited, I could see heavy snowfall through the window."
July 2026: "only nine counter seats (non-smoking, while the outdoor terrace is smoking-friendly). The walls are lined with LP records. The menu is a charming wooden dice shape."

kyoto_thai_esan_imadegawa.gf_detail: Ask: rice dishes such as khao man gai and many curries may be wheat-free, but soy and oyster sauces, fried dishes and wheat-noodle dishes are on the 100-plus menu (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_thai_esan_imadegawa.vegan_detail: Ask: Tabelog lists vegan and vegetarian options among the 100-plus dishes; fish sauce is otherwise standard (Tabelog).
kyoto_thai_esan_imadegawa.hours_raw: Tabelog: 11:00–14:30 (last entry 14:20) and 17:00–22:00 (last entry 21:50); closed Tuesday and at New Year. Weekday and weekend lunch buffet ¥1,600 (Tabelog) — ¥1,650 incl. tax on 7 November 2026 (official site), with an extra free dish per person on weekends and holidays (October 2026); buffet seats may be limited to an hour when busy. kyoto_thai_esan_imadegawa.notes: [Thai · Imadegawa, the Isan lunch buffet by Doshisha] A long-established Isan-style Thai restaurant a minute from Imadegawa Station: a ¥1,650 lunch buffet that fills up, more than 100 dishes marked by heat, vegan options, and a tatami annex in a townhouse for groups. Some found the buffet variety limited and slow to refill (March 2026) and the serving area cramped (October 2026); the som tam can hit hard (April 2026). Closed Tuesday.

roles: Thai chef, not named in a source
chef_bio.background: Reviewers in 2026 call it a long-established, "pioneering" Thai restaurant in Kyoto, run by a Thai chef, with Thai-language dish names and spice levels marked on the menu, popular with students from nearby universities and repeat locals. The official site offers a townhouse annex like a ryokan room, and take-away of over 100 dishes. The domain of the Demachiyanagi Thai restaurant Kroon now serves this site (fetched 6 November 2026).

anecdotes.text: March 2026: "The lunch was served buffet-style, and while the taste was decent, the variety was a bit limited. The replenishment of dishes was somewhat slow."
April 2026: "be cautious with the spice level! The green papaya salad… towards the end, it became particularly spicy and salty."
August 2026: with the buffet full, "I was kindly guided to the traditional house next door for a la carte orders."

kyoto_champon_matsuo_kitashirakawa.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat champon noodles and fried sara-udon noodles (2023–2026 reviews).
kyoto_champon_matsuo_kitashirakawa.vegan_detail: Not vegan: kombu-based broth with fish paste, a little pork and seafood (2023–2026 reviews).
kyoto_champon_matsuo_kitashirakawa.hours_raw: Tabelog: 11:30–14:30 and 17:00–20:30; closed Saturday. Reservations taken (Tabelog). 20 seats — two tables for eight and more (March 2024). Non-smoking. kyoto_champon_matsuo_kitashirakawa.notes: [Champon · Kitashirakawa, a vegetable-piled Showa noodle shop] A Showa-era shop at the Kitashirakawa bus stop serving just two things — champon and sara udon — buried under wok-fried cabbage and vegetables in a light, kombu-tasting salt sauce, for ¥800 regular. Some found it bland and added vinegar and mustard (February 2025); another found the sara udon a touch salty (February 2024). Cash only; closed Saturday.

chef_bio.background: Reviewers from 2023 to 2026 describe a nostalgic Showa-era interior that has not changed in decades, a menu that is still mainly champon and sara udon, lines in the past and quieter lunches now, and a shop that closed for a time and reopened (April 2026).

kyoto_chuka_soba_kodai.notes: [Ramen · off Horikawa-Nakadachiuri, ¥800 with rice] A one-person ramen shop in a narrow lane east of Horikawa, serving light, old-fashioned shoyu or shio ramen with generous chashu — ¥800 with or without rice, ¥1,000 with a mini gyudon or karaage. Cash only; closed Thursday.

chef_bio.background: Reviewers describe a one-person operation (October 2025; December 2025) and an everyday taste that a regular would never tire of (August 2025).

anecdotes.text: A regular living nearby bought the homemade yakibuta to make ramen at home (September 2026).

kyoto_doumu_imadegawa.hours_raw: Tuesday–Sunday and holidays 11:00–18:30; closed Monday and some Sundays; hours may change (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog; January 2026). 19 seats: three tables for 4, one for 5, and piano seating (Tabelog). Cakes to take away — ask inside (Tabelog; December 2024). About 2 min on foot from the Kawaramachi-Imadegawa bus stop, 6 min from Demachiyanagi (Tabelog).
kyoto_doumu_imadegawa.notes: [Cakes and tarts · Imadegawa near Demachiyanagi, since 1980] An antique-filled cake house with vintage clocks, classical music and a piano, making seasonal fruit tarts with old-style custard and a crisp crust — the fruit goes on after you order. Cake sets, take-away cakes (about ¥600), and sometimes a tune from the owner on the piano. Cash only; closed Monday.

chef_bio.background: Reviewers date the shop to 1980 (August 2025; January 2026). A longtime customer recalls a take-away showcase out front that was turned into an eat-in dessert house a few years ago (December 2024). Regulars mention the owner playing the piano for guests when the room is quiet (October 2024; July 2026).

anecdotes.text: A six-time regular looks forward to hearing the owner play the piano again (July 2026).
A December 2025 visitor arriving near 16:00 was told kindly that only 40 minutes were left before closing.

kyoto_mama_saikan_rikka.gf_detail: Ask. Northeast Chinese and Taiwanese dishes — gyoza, wontons, wonton noodles, rice vermicelli, yurinchi and karaage, pai gu pork cutlet, braised-pork rice; soy sauce and wheat wrappers throughout, and no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_mama_saikan_rikka.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options and the shop stresses fresh vegetables, and a garlic-and-salt stir-fry of seasonal vegetables appears (May 2026), but broths and sauces are not described.
kyoto_mama_saikan_rikka.hours_raw: Monday–Saturday 11:30–23:30 (L.O. 23:00); Sunday 11:30–22:00 (L.O. 21:30); closed 31 December–3 January (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; online bookings for two or more, and on Friday–Sunday online booking closes at 15:00 on the day (Tabelog). Cards (Visa, Master), e-money, PayPay, Rakuten Pay, Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog). 33 seats over two floors in a townhouse; parties of 20–50 by arrangement (Tabelog; official site). English and Chinese menus and staff (Tabelog). Student discount, ¥50 for Kyoto University students (April 2026); popular with students at lunch (May and September 2026). One minute from the Hyakumanben bus stop, 5 min from Keihan Demachiyanagi (Tabelog). Opened 1 September 2020 (Tabelog).
kyoto_mama_saikan_rikka.notes: [Chinese and Taiwanese · Hyakumanben, open until 23:30] A two-storey townhouse restaurant by Kyoto University, cooking everyday Northeast Chinese and Taiwanese dishes — gyoza with lemon salt, wonton noodles, yurinchi, pai gu — as cheap lunch sets with brown rice, and staying open until 23:30 for drinks and banquets. Busy with students at lunch; English menu.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog’s invoice number T4810789578458 is registered to the individual 高橋 義弘 (NTA register). The shop’s Tabelog text says the menu was created by the owner, a Chinese chef with 50 years of experience, around “Chinese dishes that mothers make for children every day”. Tabelog’s name search lists two other shops called Mama Saikan; no source opened links those shops to this one.
chef_bio.philosophy: Chinese dishes that mothers cook for children every day — tasty and healthy, with fresh vegetables and few chemical seasonings (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: A May 2026 diner found the brown rice so good it outshone the yurinchi.
A May 2026 visitor arriving around 22:00 was relieved to find it still open when nearby places had closed.

kyoto_bistro_cerisier.gf_detail: Ask. Regional French plates — pâtés, salads, quenelles with Nantua sauce, cassoulet, choucroute, braised beef cheek, game; bread is served at every table and gluten is not mentioned (Michelin Guide; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_bistro_cerisier.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a meat-and-charcuterie bistro — pâtés, duck, sausages, venison, frog legs, fish mousse with crayfish sauce (Michelin Guide; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_bistro_cerisier.hours_raw: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 8:30–14:00 and 18:00–21:30; Thursday 8:30–14:00; Saturday and Sunday 18:00–21:30; hours may change (Tabelog; Michelin Guide). Dinner is à la carte only (Tabelog). Reservations by phone, opening one month ahead; weekends fill fast (Tabelog; September and December 2025). Payment: the shop’s own note on Tabelog says cash only, though Tabelog’s payment field says cards are accepted — bring cash. Bread and butter are served as a table charge (September 2025). 17 seats with a counter (Tabelog). Two minutes on foot from Keihan Demachiyanagi Station (Tabelog).
kyoto_bistro_cerisier.notes: [French bistro · Demachiyanagi, regional classics to share] A small, antique-filled bistro by Demachiyanagi Station, listed in the Michelin Guide, cooking hearty French regional dishes — pâtés, quenelles, cassoulet, choucroute, game — in big portions meant for sharing, with a long regional wine list. Book by phone a month ahead; à la carte at dinner; bring cash.

chef_bio.background: The Michelin Guide says the bistro is the work of a madame captivated by French cuisine who gave shape to a longing for the real thing, in an antique interior with the feel of a country bistro. Reviewers describe a sommelier lady running the dining room (September 2025) and two women serving (December 2025); a regular’s first review dates from February 2011.
chef_bio.specialty: Regional French dishes — quenelles, cassoulet, choucroute.

anecdotes.text: A September 2025 party of three booked a holiday dinner a month ahead and found the house full that night.
A July 2026 regular, turned away from the mussels on the previous visit, finally got the mussels.
